title: Piyush Kumar
text:
Climate · Health · Evidence for development finance
I started my career measuring whether health programmes work. Now I sit on the funder side, helping decide where climate money goes. My job is to bring evidence discipline to climate and health investment decisions.
I am a Portfolio Manager at a climate action advisory in New Delhi. I work on programme design, monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) frameworks, partner due diligence and portfolio oversight for climate investments across India and the Global South. Before this, I designed outcome frameworks for a Global South climate philanthropy.
At Sambodhi Research and Communications (2018–19 and 2022–25), I led MEL and evaluation work on programmes funded by the Gates Foundation, Gavi, USAID and the World Bank in India, Bangladesh and Cambodia. The work ranged from a 36,000-household maternal and child health survey in Uttar Pradesh, to zero-dose immunisation strategy across 143 districts, to a patient-pathways tool for the World Bank’s health systems programme in Gujarat.
My research combines large household surveys (NFHS, NSSO, DHS) with satellite climate data. I ask who bears the health and financial costs of illness and of a warming climate. Current work looks at how extreme heat affects frontline health workers’ home visits after childbirth, and at inequality in hospitalisation among older Indians.
I hold a five-year integrated MA in Development Studies from IIT Madras. I work in Stata, R, Python and QGIS.
